title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen (GQA/MQA tuning, kernel & scheduling fixes)
author: Avery Liu
release_notes: Runtime: Model-specific optimizations for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen including kernel selection, scheduling heuristics, KV-cache improvements, and GQA/MQA tuning. Expected latency and throughput improvements; rollout via canary with metrics gating.
description: Motivation: Several model-specific quirks (Llama causal attention layout, Mistral short-context kernel patterns, Qwen KV-layout/quantization sensitivity) were causing suboptimal kernel selection, elevated tail latency, and lower KV-cache hit efficiency. This PR introduces targeted runtime changes to improve latency and throughput while preserving model correctness. Summary: 1) Kernel selector enhancements to prefer fused causal-attention kernels for Llama when sequence length > 1024 and bfloat16 paths available, and to prefer Mistral small-seq kernels for short-context queries to reduce launch overhead. 2) Scheduler heuristics updated to prefer model-aware batching: continuous-batcher now uses per-model average token cost and recent latency percentiles to form batches that respect SLOs while increasing batch packing. 3) KV-cache: fixed a subtle Qwen KV layout mismatch that caused partial cache misses for MQA variants; introduced stricter cache key (model-variant+prompt-hash) and soft-eviction policy to retain hot prefixes. 4) GQA/MQA tuning: add new quantization profiles and scale adjustments to reduce numeric noise for Qwen MQA and to enable lower-memory GQA runs with <1% output delta on eval prompts. Implementation notes: adds kernel hints in runtime/kernel_selector.cc, continuous batching changes in runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp, KV cache fixes in runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager.cpp and introduces quant profiles under runtime/quantization/profiles/*. Tests and validation: microbench suite (tests/benchmark/bench_llama_mistral_qwen.py) run against canary hardware; automated unit tests added for KV cache keying and quant decoding. Perf: Llama 7B: median latency -12% at 2048 tokens, p95 -9%; Mistral 7B: throughput +20% in short-context workloads; Qwen 14B MQA: memory down ~10%, p95 latency -7%, KV-cache effective hit rate improved from 78% to 89%. Backwards compatibility: changes default kernel selection only when model profile indicates compatibility; quant profiles are opt-in per-deployment. Rollout plan: canary 5% for 24h -> 25% for 48h -> 100% with automatic rollback if p95 tail latency increases >10% or token error rate increases. Checklist: [x] kernel selector tests added [x] scheduler unit tests [x] KV-cache unit and integration tests [x] perf benchmarks run and recorded [x] docs updated [x] canary rollout plan documented Related: ENG-4281 addresses observed Qwen MQA noise; ENG-4339 requested scheduler batching improvements.

review_comments: Samir Patel: Can you clarify the fallback ordering if fused causal kernel fails on a particular GPU? Author: runtime falls back to generic attention kernel with identical outputs; added explicit test and logging for fallback path.

Elena García: KV-keying change could increase cache fragmentation, any mitigation? Author: added soft-eviction LRU policy and grouping by model-variant+prefix-hash to reduce fragmentation; included microbench that shows hit-rate improvement.

Marcus Chen: How was quant profile validated for hallucination/regression? Author: ran eval harness against 2k curated prompts and validated <1% BLEU/EM deltas; included eval artifacts in CI artifacts and performance dashboard.

CI bot: Perf check initially flagged a 3% regression on a specific Mistral long-context test causing a rerun. Author: adjusted selector heuristics to detect long-context pattern and re-ran perf; subsequent runs passed and showed improved throughput for short-context workloads.
